title: Mutual Induction Tour
description: Guided walkthrough of the primary current, the shared core flux, the turns ratio, and what the coupling coefficient k costs you.

steps.title: Two coils that never touch
steps.body: Primary and secondary windings sit on opposite limbs of one laminated core. No wire runs between them — everything that crosses does so as magnetic flux. This is the textbook two-winding model, an ODE in the two loop currents, not a field solve.

steps.title: Step 1 — the primary current I_p
steps.body: The drive slider sets the primary supply. Current I_p in the left winding is what the whole device runs on; the winding glow tracks it. Raise the drive and watch V_p swing — the primary is an inductor with resistance, so I_p lags the applied voltage rather than following it instantly.

steps.title: Step 2 — flux in the core
steps.body: I_p magnetises the steel limbs, and the flux runs around the closed core to the other side. The core glow is the normalised flux. Only a *changing* flux induces anything, which is why the drive here is AC: hold the current still and the secondary goes dead.

steps.title: Step 3 — the secondary and the turns ratio
steps.body: The changing flux drives an EMF in the right-hand winding, and the load resistor turns it into current I_s. V_s / V_p follows the turns ratio: more turns buys voltage and costs current. Power out never exceeds power in — this model conserves it, minus the resistive losses it does carry.

steps.title: Step 4 — coupling k, and leakage
steps.body: M = k·√(L_p·L_s): the coupling coefficient k says what fraction of the primary's flux actually reaches the secondary. Press Leakage to drop k and watch V_s fall while I_p does not — the missing flux closes through air instead of the core. That gap is the difference between the ideal transformer and a real one.

steps.title: What this model is not
steps.body: Two coupled loop equations with a scalar k. No magnetic saturation, no hysteresis loop, no eddy currents, no winding geometry, no FEM anywhere. k is a dial you turn, not a number computed from the core — a teaching model of mutual induction, not a transformer design tool.
